title: Intervention-surface lockout breaks recursive self-intervention closure

scientific_object.broad_claim: Recursive/self-referential agents can improve their own scaffold or tools.
scientific_object.narrow_claim: When the capability used for self-reading, self-writing, and self-verification itself enters the fault domain, under what conditions does read-write-verify recursive closure break, and can a strictly bounded out-of-band repair side-channel restore that closure?

closest_work_boundary.collision_watch_only: self-harness/self-modification x runtime tool failure/fault injection x repair side-channel
covered_by_existing_work: DGM: recursive code self-modification and inherited self-modification capability
SICA: coding agent edits itself using coding tools
POLARIS: inspect policy/traces, produce persistent policy patch, continue
Self-Harness: prompts, tools, and execution harness are mutable optimization objects
runtime tool-failure benchmarks: availability denial, silent no-op, corrupted state, schema mismatch, retry/fallback/verification
closest_work_boundary.surviving_intersection: The intervention capability responsible for self-inspection, self-modification, or self-verification is itself the faulted resource, rather than an ordinary task tool.

why_close: The source tree is mounted into the agent sandbox at /workspace/exo and is intended to be readable and modifiable by the agent.
Canonical event history is host-side/outside the sandbox and survives ordinary restart/rewind, giving an external lineage domain.
The default harness exposes shell-class execution plus a host-side rebuild/restart capability, so self-intervention is a real multi-path capability surface rather than a single write_file tool.
The project is actively discussing canonical writer/harness identity when harness mutability is allowed, which is adjacent to the recursive trust boundary required here.

source_scan.policy: Do not treat the July pin as the current main SHA; acquire an exact upstream pin before any Exo-specific pilot.

R.object: self source/state needed to diagnose the intervention surface
equivalent_paths: Python or other interpreter reads over /workspace/exo
host-side canonical event introspection where exposed
R.reason: No exhaustive Exo-specific read mediation has been demonstrated.

W.object: persistent self source/tool state that changes the recursive object
W.reason: A read-only bind mount with no Docker socket and all Linux capabilities dropped blocked every enumerated direct file-write path; tool-name denial and same-owner mode bits did not.

V.object: the mechanism that establishes whether a self-edit is valid and makes it active
equivalent_paths: other build/test endpoints reachable through unrestricted shell
V.reason: Disabling one verifier/restart tool leaves shell-equivalent build/test paths; no verifier firewall has yet mediated the whole class.

dry_run.scientific_interpretation: The dry-run falsifies tool-name and chmod-style W lockout as capability boundaries and establishes that a resource-level read-only boundary can block the enumerated W-equivalent paths. It does not establish full recursive closure lockout because R and V remain unqualified.

promotion_gates.pass_rule: Enumerate functionally equivalent R/W/V paths and demonstrate that the full-lockout arm cannot bypass the intended fault through shell, interpreters, patch/git plumbing, tool-management state, rebuild/restart, or another host API.
promotion_gates.current_result: W resource-boundary mechanism supported; full R/W/V class lockout not yet qualified.

promotion_gates.pass_rule: The modified harness/code persists across generations while checkpoint, lineage, and evaluator remain outside the fault domain; the supervisor may only restore a predeclared primitive and may not author the repair.

No-fault sustains R-to-W-to-V; intervention-surface lockout collapses closure; the minimal out-of-band primitive restores it; fixed-agent, history-only reflection, and hidden redundant-tool controls do not recover equally.

next_gate.name: EXO_SPECIFIC_VERIFICATION_FIREWALL_AND_FULL_RWV_DRY_RUN
design: Treat SELF_SRC, SELF_TOOL_STATE, CANONICAL_LOG, and BUILD_VERIFY_ENDPOINT as separately labeled resources.
Keep canonical lineage/evaluator outside the recursive fault domain.
Use the demonstrated resource-level boundary for W rather than tool-name denial.
Interpose V at the build/test/restart endpoint so shell cannot reproduce verification through an alternate route.
Expose exactly one predeclared out-of-band repair primitive whose semantics are restoration of capability, not authoring a repair patch.

projection_policy.reason: RSI-C01 remains shadow/HOLD until all substrate gates pass.
